title: CI/CD separates build from release
points: Continuous integration builds and tests each commit.
Continuous delivery holds an immutable releasable artifact; approval can gate production.
CodePipeline orchestrates actions, while production health needs separate verification.
remember: CodePipeline orchestrates actions, while production health needs separate verification.

title: Choose the right CI/CD service
points: CodeCommit or a connected Git provider supplies source; CodeBuild tests/packages.
CodePipeline orchestrates stages; CodeDeploy manages eligible rollouts.
ECR stores container images; CloudFormation provisions infrastructure.
remember: ECR stores container images; CloudFormation provisions infrastructure.

title: CodePipeline stages and action boundaries
points: Source, build, test and deploy actions exchange versioned artifacts.
A failed stage stops downstream promotion; manual approvals gate later stages.
Action roles and artifact stores define account and Region boundaries.
remember: Action roles and artifact stores define account and Region boundaries.

title: CodeBuild turns source into evidence
points: A buildspec defines install, pre_build, build and post_build phases.
The CodeBuild service role accesses source, secrets and artifact destinations.
Test reports and immutable output are evidence; build success is not runtime health.
remember: Test reports and immutable output are evidence; build success is not runtime health.

title: Connect Git without hidden credentials
points: CodeCommit is available to new customers; connected providers use AWS CodeConnections.
Scope repository access and the pipeline source action; verify event triggers.
Avoid embedding long-lived source credentials in the pipeline.
remember: Avoid embedding long-lived source credentials in the pipeline.

title: Separate DEV and PROD release paths
points: DEV tests and deploys a candidate; PROD promotes the same reviewed artifact.
Separate accounts and roles contain blast radius; approval checks evidence.
Canary alarms and rollback verify the production release.
remember: Canary alarms and rollback verify the production release.

title: Manual approval is a deliberate release gate
points: A manual approval action pauses the pipeline before the next stage.
Review build/test, scan, artifact identity and rollback readiness.
Approval is a decision gate, not a production health test.
remember: Approval is a decision gate, not a production health test.

title: Scan and sign the deployable image
points: Build and scan an immutable container digest before promotion.
Sign and attest provenance; keep signing permissions distinct from deployment.
Signing does not prove the image has no vulnerabilities.
remember: Signing does not prove the image has no vulnerabilities.

title: Promote across accounts with scoped roles
points: Tooling account stores artifacts and assumes a scoped production deployment role.
Trust policy determines who assumes the role; permissions define allowed actions.
Cross-account artifact and KMS grants are required for access.
remember: Cross-account artifact and KMS grants are required for access.

title: Cross-Region pipelines need regional stores
points: A pipeline has a home Region and needs an artifact store in each action Region.
Cross-Region action roles, encryption keys and artifact replication must align.
A cross-Region action is deployed in its target Region, not magically global.
remember: A cross-Region action is deployed in its target Region, not magically global.

title: CodeDeploy targets and deployment types
points: CodeDeploy supports EC2/on-premises, Lambda and ECS deployment targets.
In-place and blue/green apply according to target platform; choose traffic shifting carefully.
Rollback support depends on deployment configuration and alarms.
remember: Rollback support depends on deployment configuration and alarms.

title: EC2 in-place deploy in batches
points: EC2 in-place updates existing instances in batches via AppSpec hooks.
Validate lifecycle hooks and target health before the next batch.
Rollback redeploys a revision and does not undo external side effects.
remember: Rollback redeploys a revision and does not undo external side effects.

title: ASG blue/green preserves an old fleet
points: Blue/green creates a replacement Auto Scaling group or fleet while preserving old capacity.
Test the green environment before shifting production traffic.
Keep the old fleet for a defined rollback window, accounting for double capacity cost.
remember: Keep the old fleet for a defined rollback window, accounting for double capacity cost.

title: Lambda alias canary and linear shifts
points: Lambda aliases weight traffic between published versions.
Canary and linear CodeDeploy configurations shift gradually with hooks and alarms.
An alarm can restore the prior version, but side effects remain.
remember: An alarm can restore the prior version, but side effects remain.

title: ECS blue/green uses two task sets
points: ECS blue/green creates a replacement task set behind a second target group.
A listener shifts traffic after tests; alarms can stop and roll back.
Task definition, health checks and data compatibility all affect success.
remember: Task definition, health checks and data compatibility all affect success.

title: Compare rollout curves and rollback
points: All-at-once is fast but exposes all traffic immediately; canary limits initial exposure.
Linear shifts in increments; rolling replaces fleet members in batches.
Choose a strategy using blast radius, capacity, observability and state migration.
remember: Choose a strategy using blast radius, capacity, observability and state migration.

title: Credential leak response begins at commit
points: Commit and pipeline events can trigger secret scanning.
Redact findings and revoke or rotate exposed credentials with scoped automation.
Notify the owner, retain audit evidence and prevent recurrence with short-lived roles.
remember: Notify the owner, retain audit evidence and prevent recurrence with short-lived roles.

title: CodeGuru Reviewer is legacy context
points: CodeGuru Reviewer existing associations remain usable; new associations stopped November 7, 2025.
Amazon Q Developer supplies current code review and security analysis.
CodeGuru Profiler addresses runtime performance, not source review.
remember: CodeGuru Profiler addresses runtime performance, not source review.

title: EC2 Image Builder promotes tested AMIs
points: EC2 Image Builder composes, hardens and tests an AMI.
Promote a tested AMI version across accounts and Regions, then update launch templates.
Roll the fleet in waves with health gates and a prior-image rollback path.
remember: Roll the fleet in waves with health gates and a prior-image rollback path.

title: SAM release uses the same pipeline gates
points: CodeBuild tests/packages a SAM application; CloudFormation expands the SAM transform.
CodeDeploy shifts Lambda alias traffic using hooks and alarms.
Integration tests must exercise deployed API Gateway, Lambda and DynamoDB behavior.
remember: Integration tests must exercise deployed API Gateway, Lambda and DynamoDB behavior.

title: Bedrock evaluation is a release gate
points: Pin prompt, model, configuration and representative dataset versions.
Compare automatic metrics with human judgments for quality, safety, cost and latency.
Block promotion when thresholds fail and monitor drift after release.
remember: Block promotion when thresholds fail and monitor drift after release.

title: Evaluate RAG answers and failure cases
points: Test representative and adversarial queries with reference answers.
Separate retrieval relevance, answer quality and grounding; review ambiguous cases.
Version the dataset, model and knowledge base index with results.
remember: Version the dataset, model and knowledge base index with results.

title: Walkthrough: cross-account image release
points: Build and test a pinned source revision in tooling.
Scan, sign and attest the immutable ECR image digest.
Assume a scoped production role, approve promotion, canary and check alarms.
remember: Assume a scoped production role, approve promotion, canary and check alarms.

title: Walkthrough: failed canary rollback
points: A 10% canary exposes elevated errors and triggers a CloudWatch alarm.
CodeDeploy restores routing to the healthy version and verifies recovery.
Traffic rollback does not reverse writes, messages or schema changes.
remember: Traffic rollback does not reverse writes, messages or schema changes.

title: Choose the release service by job
points: CodePipeline | Orchestrate stages and approvals | Source → build → test → deploy | Coordinate the release
CodeBuild | Build and test in managed compute | Source + buildspec → artifacts | Compile, test, package
CodeDeploy | Deploy application revisions | Artifact → EC2, Lambda or ECS | Traffic shift and rollback
CodeArtifact | Store packages and dependencies | Package version → repository | Govern reusable packages
remember: Pipeline orchestrates; build creates artifacts; deploy changes running workloads.

title: Choose a rollout by risk and rollback
points: All at once | Replace all capacity together | Small or tolerant workloads | Fast rollout, largest blast radius
Rolling | Replace batches in place | Capacity can shrink temporarily | Track health between batches
Blue/green | New environment beside old | Fast switch and rollback | Verify green, shift traffic
Canary | Small traffic slice first | High-risk releases | Watch errors and latency before expand
remember: Match release pattern to blast radius, capacity headroom, health signals and recovery time.

title: Place release gates at the right boundary
points: Source | Secret scan, reviewed change | Reject compromised commit | Revoke leaked credential
Build | Tests, image scan, SBOM | Promote immutable artifact | Fix and rebuild
Pre-deploy | Policy, template, approval | Permit scoped rollout | Block unsafe change
Post-deploy | Canary health, SLOs, alarms | Expand or stop traffic shift | Roll back and investigate
remember: A passing build does not prove a healthy production release.
